Landscape acceptance — October 16, 2026

The bounded native Landscape extension passed its initial and extended real MCP acceptance tests in UE 5.6.1. This is development acceptance for isolated test maps; production-level editing and World Partition mutation remain unsupported.

Verified identity and delivered state

  • Live session: unreal-3960.
  • Project: [local path].
  • Saved map: /Game/ForgeMCPTests/Landscape/L_TerrainAcceptance_20261016_v2.
  • Landscape: one component, 63 quads per section, one subsection, 64 × 64 vertices.
  • XY scale: 100 cm; Z scale: 100. Footprint: 63 × 63 metres.
  • Native Edit Layer: ForgeTerrain.
  • Final state: completed, persistence_validated:true, dirty:false, layers_up_to_date:true.
  • Final layer height MD5: 4345b7bd2cfad75367fe31b085864072.
  • Final local height range after flattening/smoothing: -492.1875 to 353.90625 cm.

The separate original editor remained on /Game/Levels/L_City_World_Master.L_City_World_Master, with PIE stopped. SHA-256 comparisons verified all 851 protected city/Sky files unchanged. No roads, buildings or nine-kilometre city terrain were generated.

Evidence gates

Gate Result
Python full suite 392 passed.
Latest affected Python/stdio contract checks 14 passed after the frame API addition.
Ruff Passed for server, new test and acceptance runner.
Native compilation Full plugin/runtime compilation and linking passed.
Editor target UnrealEditor Win64 Development passed; final incremental target also passed.
Real MCP subprocess Creation, hill, valley, flatten, smooth, generation, coastline, explicit heightmap, save/reload and cancellation passed.
Height validation Every completed stage matched exact planned native height samples; completed job checksums matched previews.
Persistence Native save/reload passed twice. Landscape GUID, layer GUID, dimensions and exact height samples matched.
Read-only inspection Repeated inspection preserved a clean reloaded map.
Viewport Intermediate and completed native viewport captures inspected; terrain framing corrected. Unlit geometry review mode is used.
Protection 851 before/after protected-file hashes matched; city editor retained its original world.
World Partition Inspection metadata supported; mutations and external actor/streaming package saving explicitly rejected, not validated.

The hill reached +800 cm and the valley reached -500 cm before the flatten/smooth passes. Flattening blended its selected rectangle to +200 cm; smoothing used the pre-edit neighborhood data. Every edit recorded multiple observable progress states. Generated terrain used a deterministic sine field; coastline testing used an X-axis elevation ramp. The explicit heightmap test applied a 4 × 4 sample patch.

One-use preview replay and native height-range rejection passed. Cancellation stopped a 64-row job after 3 rows, preserved an actual partial height change, and applied no more rows during the subsequent observation. It did not claim rollback. The retained backup path is recorded in the JSON acceptance report. The test reset its extra terrain experiments, reconstructed the hill/valley example and required the final saved/reloaded height checksum to match the first successful persistence check.

Performance limits

Observed maximum native stage times across the 12 completed edit jobs ranged from 2.527 to 8.543 ms. The default stage was four rows with a 0.3-second interval. These measurements cover the native batch operation; they do not establish overall frame rate, GPU cost, large-terrain performance or production World Partition responsiveness. Import, save and reload remain bounded synchronous native calls.

Resolved failures and remaining scope

The first run failed at reload because Unreal's editing-interface read helper calls Texture->Modify(), dirtying a package during inspection. The read path now copies texture source mip data without the editing interface; clean-package regression checks passed. Native bounds-based framing replaced generic actor framing. The stricter creation guard was also corrected to ignore Unreal-created transient debug helpers while rejecting authored actors. Earlier failure evidence is retained under Saved/LandscapeDevelopment/attempt1/ and attempt2-guard/.

This extension currently supports only bounded disposable maps, one ForgeTerrain Edit Layer, at most 127 × 127 vertices/four components, rectangular vertex edits and explicit heightmap patches of at most 256 samples. Multi-layer composition, independent layers per stroke, image-file heightmap import/export, erosion, water/coastal simulation, World Partition proxy creation/unloaded cells and production-level mutation remain unsupported. The single-component 64 × 64 case is the live acceptance case; other supported topology combinations have not all received individual live tests. Large-world and physics/PIE acceptance are not claimed.

Source, backups and installation state

The engine-wide source-authoritative plugin contains the new native source; its running installed DLL was not replaced. The validated binary is currently loaded only by the isolated LiveHost editor. The existing city session still runs the earlier engine binary. The existing client needs a fresh MCP server/tool registry to discover the five new tools; the acceptance runner used a fresh real stdio server. A future engine-wide binary installation/restart is separate from this isolated validation and was not performed on the open city editor.

Native sources match across build host, live host and the engine source tree. Original affected source files are backed up under Saved/LandscapeDevelopment/SourceBackup-20261016/. The complete native delta is Saved/LandscapeDevelopment/native-landscape.patch; native hashes and a compiled binary receipt are beside it. No source was published or committed by this task.

Machine evidence: Saved/LandscapeDevelopment/acceptance.json, build-and-validation-receipt.json, protected-content-after.json, editor-target-first-pass.log, editor-target-final.log, and final-incremental-console.log. Viewport images are in the same folder.

See Landscape API and operation contract.
